title: The spread of vaccination
summary: In May 1796 the English physician Edward Jenner inoculated a boy with matter from a cowpox sore, the basis of vaccination against smallpox. In 1885 Louis Pasteur prevented rabies through vaccination, and Jonas Salk developed the first effective polio vaccine in 1952–55. In 1974 the World Health Organization set up its programme to bring immunization to the whole world. In 1980 the World Health Assembly declared smallpox eradicated. Immunization has saved at least 154 million lives in the past 50 years.
